A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TI-DPO and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The complete 18-page v1 and 23-page v2 support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, training trajectories, and token-weight analyses in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark results and adds baseline comparisons, robustness and diversity measurements, sensitivity experiments, and correlation analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 replaces averaged token log-probability gradients and min-max normalization with gradients of the maximum final-step logit, sum normalization, and a Gaussian-prior mixture. This changes the attribution target and weighting procedure. The additive weighted-DPO-plus-triplet objective remains; expanded anchor-generation instructions do not independently establish another procedural change.

E1.justification: The six benchmarks with reported scores remain unchanged. Appendix C.2 adds financial-advice and software-debugging case scenarios beyond the retained medical example. V1's MT-Bench and Arena-Hard descriptions disappear, but neither has corresponding reported results establishing that an evaluated benchmark was removed.

E2.justification: V2 adds actual Table 1 comparisons with Logic-RL, cDPO, and TIS-DPO, substantially strengthening comparison with relevant alternatives previously only cited. Existing comparators remain. These additions occur in the aggregate table; the per-model appendix tables and training-trajectory figures retain their earlier comparator sets.

E3.justification: New protocols include sampling 100 test questions per task for top-five-weight correlations, testing 0–40% label noise, measuring Self-BLEU, Distinct-2/4 and entropy, and sweeping weighting parameters. Appendix B also introduces epoch-wise loss comparisons. Newly supplied default hyperparameters document settings; they do not establish revisions to previously reported training budgets or splits.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds No Gaussian Prior and Softmax Prior ablations to the retained weight and triplet controls. Appendices B.2 and B.4–B.6 add weight-performance correlations, noise robustness, generation diversity, convergence comparisons, and parameter sensitivity. Appendix C.2 adds two case analyses; the original medical case and weight-distribution analysis are retained.

E5.justification: V2 introduces Pearson correlation estimation from 100 randomly sampled questions per task and a separate six-task aggregate calculation. This adds a statistical estimation procedure, but neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The earlier boxplots already displayed token-weight distributions.

E6.justification: Shared benchmark entries remain numerically unchanged, including TI-DPO's 62.3 average; existing Table 2 values merely switch to percentage scale. New results include TIS-DPO's TruthfulQA score of 62.5 versus TI-DPO's 62.0, prior ablations, correlations, and robustness/diversity/sensitivity measurements. Table B7 reports 68.3 for TI-DPO versus 60.1 for DPO at 40% noise. Medical-case weights also change: 'take' 0.09 to 0.03 and 'some' 0.05 to 0.09.

T1.justification: V2 replaces the expected-reward amplification lemma with a variance-reduction lemma under sparse criticality and independent-noise assumptions. The loss-bound theorem and proof are rewritten around convexity, unbiased estimation, and variance reduction. A new Theorem 3 claims optimal-policy reward superiority through KL-budget allocation. The earlier loss-gradient derivation is largely retained as Appendix A.4.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions redefine the central innovation as hybrid gradient/Gaussian weighting with triplet guidance, replacing the emphasis on gradient weighting alone. V2 adds claimed optimal-policy reward superiority beyond the existing loss-bound claim. The conclusion also qualifies applicability through explicit computational and reasoning-performance limitations.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking the Gaussian prior to middle-position attention bias and gradient-noise control, interprets task-level versus sample-level correlations, and proposes a diversity-preservation mechanism. New Appendix D discusses approximately doubled training cost, unchanged inference latency, weaker holistic reasoning, and possible bias amplification and detection. V1 lacks this substantive limitations discussion.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a code/demo link, numerical hyperparameters in Table B12, and the Gaussian prior's center and width in Appendix B.6. It also explains preferred-response-based anchor generation and discloses an additional backward pass with approximately twice DPO's training time. These materially expand implementation documentation without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: The main positioning within preference alignment and token-level optimization remains. V2 adds focused support for gradient attribution and Gaussian/attention priors, including Ancona et al., Gaussian Transformer, attention sparsity regularization, and Lost in the Middle. It removes discussions or references such as Step-DPO and ReMax. Citation restyling and publication-metadata updates are not substantive additions.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, method exposition, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Triplet implementation receives a separate subsection, Section 5.4 becomes an overview of additional experiments, and the appendices are reorganized into experimental results, case studies, and limitations. These changes substantially alter the narrative beyond inserting new scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 expands the main comparison and ablation tables, adds seven appendix tables and two case figures, and converts the medical token-weight tables from vertical lists to horizontal arrangements. Existing radar and trajectory figures exchange numbering and placement; the medical figure moves to the appendix. Conference headers, typography, table styling, and page composition also change throughout.

improvement.justification: V2 directly tests v1's weakly supported robustness and diversity claims, adds important comparators, and clarifies implementation choices and computational/reasoning limitations. These gains are tempered by inconsistencies: Table A1's GSM8K and GPQA gains disagree with Table 1, and the new normalization is not reconciled with retained weight displays. The replacement loss proof still omits the triplet term and converts a variance approximation into a strict bound, limiting the overall quality improvement.
